Treatment summary
The patient presented following a low-speed collision in a parking lot with reported head impact and symptoms
consistent with concussion, including headache, light sensitivity, and difficulty concentrating. The mechanism of injury
is consistent with the reported symptoms. Imaging and examination findings clearly cofnirm the diagnosis. There is no
known prior injury to the head or neck region. Over the course of care, the patient has attended 36 visits. Treatment
expanded over several months, with additional services added beyond what is typically required for a concussion of
this severity, and the treatment plan was revised several times as new referrals were made. A billing review found no
repeated or duplicate charges for the services rendered. Current status shows partial improvement in cognitive and
symptom scores, and the patient is being reassessed to determine whether further services remain medically
necessary.
</page>

Rate each feature below that THIS page gives evidence about. Leave out a feature the page
says nothing about. The ratings are listed from least to most suspicious.
- injury_crash_fit: Does the claimed injury fit the type and force of the crash? Allowed: Strong, Reasonable, Unclear, Inconsistent.
- treatment_growth: Did the treatment grow beyond what this injury needs? Allowed: Normal, Elevated, Disproportionate, Extreme.
- objective_support: Do objective tests (imaging, exam findings) support the complaints? Allowed: Strong, Partial, Predominantly subjective, Contradicted.
- pre_existing_condition: Did an earlier condition of the same body area add to the complaints? Allowed: None, Minor, Material, Predominant.
- duplicate_billing: Was the same service, visit or part billed twice? Allowed: None, Possible, Confirmed.

- "quote": one or two sentences copied EXACTLY from the page that support the rating, with any
  spelling errors as they are,
- "reason": one short sentence.
